subtitle: From Kangla’s red earth to the world’s green fields

panels.shot: wide, low-angle shot of Kangla fort with a dusty polo ground in the foreground, Manipuri ponies poised mid-gallop, and a faint ghosted overlay of Victorian officers watching
panels.action: King Khagemba sits regal on a low embankment at Kangla as Manipuri horsemen thunder past on compact ponies, while in the distant haze a future scene of curious British officers at Imphal Polo Ground faintly mirrors the play.

dialogue.text: From Kangla’s red earth, King Khagemba’s horse game rides through exile and empire, carrying Sagol Kangjei from a Meitei court sport to the polo fields of the world.

i18n.hi: कांगला की लाल मिट्टी से, राजा खागेम्बा का घुड़सवारी खेल निर्वासन और साम्राज्यों के साथ घूमता गया, मेइती दरबार के खेल से दुनिया के पोलो मैदानों तक सगोल कंग्जेई को ले गया।

panels.shot: slow push-in from bird’s-eye over Kangla fort, revealing the central ground
panels.action: From above, the walled complex of Kangla spreads along the Imphal river, its inner ground marked by hoof-scarred earth where small ponies churn up dust as nobles and soldiers gather around.

dialogue.text: In the early 1600s, under King Khagemba, Kangla was not only palace and fortress; within its walls, a rough horse game called Sagol Kangjei thudded across the dust, half-play, half-warfare.

i18n.hi: सत्रहवीं सदी की शुरुआत में, राजा खागेम्बा के समय, कांगला सिर्फ महल और किला नहीं था; उसकी दीवारों के भीतर सगोल कंग्जेई नाम का कड़ा घुड़सवारी खेल धूल में गूँजता था, आधा खेल, आधा युद्ध।

panels.shot: medium shot at ground level, focusing on a compact Manipuri pony rearing against a backdrop of hills and clouds
panels.action: A wiry Manipuri pony rears with flaring nostrils, short and sturdy, the valley hills rising beyond as a Meitei rider leans forward with easy balance, cane stick in hand.

dialogue.text: These were not tall warhorses of Persian tales, but the hardy Manipuri pony: small, sure-footed, shaped by the hills and swamps of Manipur, now traced in its own distinct bloodline by modern science.

i18n.hi: ये फ़ारसी किस्सों वाले ऊँचे युद्धघोड़े नहीं, बल्कि मजबूत मणिपुरी टट्टू थे: छोटे, फुर्तीले, मणिपुर की पहाड़ियों और दलदलों ने गढ़े हुए, जिनकी अलग नस्ल आज विज्ञान भी मानता है।

panels.shot: medium wide of Khagemba seated in court-side shade, watching a chaotic match
panels.action: King Khagemba, in royal attire, sits beneath a simple canopy at the edge of the ground, face intent, as horsemen crash towards a ball in a swirl of dust and tangled ponies.

dialogue.text: Khagemba’s chronicle remembers his wars and reforms, but it also notes this: the king watched Sagol Kangjei, and he changed its rules. Under him, a wild chase became an ordered court sport.

i18n.hi: खागेम्बा की दास्तानें उसकी लड़ाइयाँ और सुधार गिनती हैं, पर यह भी दर्ज है: राजा सगोल कंग्जेई देखता था, और उसने नियम बदले। उसके दौर में जंगली दौड़ एक सजा-सँवरा दरबारी खेल बनी।

panels.shot: close-up on Khagemba’s weathered face as he gestures to an attendant with a cane
panels.action: Khagemba leans forward, eyes sharp, as he signals to a scribe and a senior horseman, pointing his cane towards the field where two riders jostle dangerously close.

dialogue.text: The Cheitharol Kumbaba notes his revisions. Teams were set, seven a side. Sticks, goals, even fouls slowly took shape. What had been many village customs became a single, royal game.

i18n.hi: चैथारोल कुम्बाबा में उसके बदले हुए नियम दर्ज हैं। टीमें बनीं, सात-सात खिलाड़ी। डंडे, गोल, यहाँ तक कि फ़ाउल भी तय हुए। गाँव–गाँव की अलग रस्में मिलकर एक शाही खेल बनीं।

panels.shot: diagrammatic wide shot of players lined up, but rendered cinematically with dust and tension
panels.action: Seven horsemen in traditional Meitei attire line up on each side of the Kangla ground, ponies stamping in formation as officials stand at the center holding a cane and a small ball.

dialogue.text: Now, Sagol Kangjei began in order. Seven riders faced seven riders; positions were known, starting formations fixed. War-trained men learned to read space, timing and their comrades’ movements.

i18n.hi: अब सगोल कंग्जेई तरह से शुरू होती। सात सवार सात के सामने; जगहें तय, शुरुआत की कतार पक्की। युद्ध–सिखे सिपाही मैदान, समय और साथियों की चाल पढ़ने लगे।

panels.shot: dynamic tracking shot alongside galloping riders mid-play
panels.action: Ponies race shoulder to shoulder as a Meitei rider leans low to hook the ball with a cane stick, his teammates spreading wide while a crowded Kangla gallery of nobles and soldiers watches.

dialogue.text: In the king’s eyes, it was drill as much as delight. This thunder of hooves taught balance, control and comradeship. A prince learned to fall without fear; a soldier to surge and withdraw on signal.

i18n.hi: राजा की नज़र में यह जितना मौज थी, उतनी ही मशक। टापों की गरज से संतुलन, काबू और साथ निभाना सीखा गया। राजकुमार बेख़ौफ़ गिरना सीखता, सिपाही इशारे पर टूटना और लौटना।

panels.shot: wide shot of the Imphal Polo Ground generations later, echoing Kangla
panels.action: Centuries later, beyond Kangla’s walls, horsemen play on the open Imphal Polo Ground, the same compact ponies and curved sticks now framed by a broader valley sky and more varied onlookers.

dialogue.text: Time moved. Kings changed, the valley opened, but the game stayed. From Kangla’s inner court it spilled into the larger Imphal ground, carried by nobles, warriors and common riders alike.

i18n.hi: समय बदला। राजा बदले, घाटी खुली, पर खेल बना रहा। कांगला के भीतरी आँगन से निकलकर वह बड़े इम्फाल मैदान तक फैल गया, रजवाड़ों, योद्धाओं और आम सवारों के साथ।

panels.shot: somber wide shot of Manipuri horsemen on the move eastward through forest, distant pagoda outlines hinting at Burma
panels.action: A file of Manipuri riders, ponies laden, moves silently through dense forest; in the far distance, a Burmese-style pagoda rises through the mist, hinting at a foreign land.

dialogue.text: War and exile also carried their horses. Burmese chronicles and modern historians note Manipuri riders—Cassay horsemen—in Burmese service, deported east yet still bound to their ponies.

i18n.hi: युद्ध और निर्वासन भी इन घोड़ों को साथ ले गए। बर्मी ग्रंथों और आज के इतिहासकारों ने मणिपुरी सवारों को दर्ज किया है—कस्से घुड़सवार—जो बर्मा की फ़ौज में गए, पर अपने टट्टुओं से ही बंधे रहे।

panels.shot: mid shot of a Manipuri rider in foreign service playing a rough game on ponies with comrades, informal yet intense
panels.action: Among a mixed company of riders in a Burmese frontier post, a Manipuri horseman urges his pony after a ball, improvised cane in hand, while curious comrades laugh and join the chase.

dialogue.text: In camps and garrisons beyond Manipur, they played their valley game on foreign soil. Sagol Kangjei became part memory, part training, a reminder of home etched in dust and sweat.

i18n.hi: मणिपुर से दूर डेरों और छावनियों में भी वे अपनी घाटी का खेल पराई ज़मीन पर खेलते। सगोल कंग्जेई आधा याद, आधा अभ्यास रहा, घर की मिट्टी और पसीने से बना निशान।

panels.shot: wide shot of the Imphal Polo Ground in the mid-19th century with British officers observing from the sidelines
panels.action: On the Imphal ground in the 1850s, Manipuri horsemen gallop in full play while a small group of British officers in uniforms stand at the edge, shading their eyes, intent and intrigued.

dialogue.text: By the mid-nineteenth century, new eyes watched. British officers on India’s eastern frontier, many already mounted men, saw Sagol Kangjei at Imphal and nearby, a fast, tightly played pony game.

i18n.hi: उन्नीसवीं सदी के बीच तक नए दर्शक आ चुके थे। भारत की पूरबी सीमा के ब्रिटिश अफ़सर, जो खुद घुड़सवार थे, इम्फाल और आसपास सगोल कंग्जेई देखने लगे—तेज़, कसा हुआ टट्टू खेल।

panels.shot: medium shot of a seasoned Manipuri player (Keifa Singh) mid-swing, framed against watching British officers
panels.action: A veteran Manipuri rider, identified by tradition as Keifa Singh, leans low in the saddle to send the ball flying, his face calm, while British officers behind exchange astonished glances.

dialogue.text: Manipuri tradition names one such master, Keifa Singh, whose skill impressed these newcomers. Whether every tale around him can be proved or not, the effect is clear: British officers were captivated.

i18n.hi: मणिपुरी परंपरा एक उस्ताद का नाम याद रखती है—कैफ़ा सिंह—जिसकी कला ने इन नवागंतुकों को चकित किया। हर किस्सा सही हो या नहीं, असर साफ़ है: ब्रिटिश अफ़सर मोहित हो गए।

panels.shot: close-up on a British officer’s notebook in hand, with a sketch of field layout and notes, Manipuri riders blurred behind
panels.action: A British officer holds a small notebook, a rough sketch of the ground and positions visible on the open page, as the blurred forms of Manipuri players gallop in the background.

dialogue.text: They asked questions, watched rules enforced, marked team numbers, field lengths, striking techniques. From this valley codification, they took ideas north and west, into their own regimental games.

i18n.hi: उन्होंने सवाल पूछे, नियमों को लागू होते देखा, टीम की गिनती, मैदान की लंबाई, मारने के ढंग नोट किए। इस घाटी के बनाए नियमों से वे ख़याल उठा ले गए, उत्तर और पश्चिम, अपनी रेजिमेंटों के खेलों में।

panels.shot: split visual: foreground Manipuri pony under rider; background faint silhouette of taller cavalry horses in British cantonment
panels.action: A Manipuri pony stands alert in the foreground, reins held by a local rider, while in the hazy background taller British cavalry horses loom, riders discussing and measuring the smaller animal.

dialogue.text: Even the pony left its mark. Early British polo rules abroad limited pony height—echoes of these compact Manipuri mounts, whose size had shaped the speed and style of the original game.

i18n.hi: टट्टू ने भी अपनी छाप छोड़ी। बाहर बने शुरुआती ब्रिटिश पोलो नियमों में टट्टू की ऊँचाई पर रोक थी—इन्हीं नाप के मणिपुरी टट्टुओं की गूँज, जिनकी कद-काठी ने मूल खेल की रफ़्तार और रंग तय किए थे।

panels.shot: wide shot of a British-Indian regiment playing polo on a new ground, with a Manipuri rider watching from the edge
panels.action: On a broad field in Assam or Cachar, British and Indian officers in mixed dress gallop after a ball, while at the edge a Manipuri rider, arms folded, watches with a small, unreadable smile.

dialogue.text: Soon, in Cachar and Assam, regimental polo clubs formed. The British would call the sport theirs in new lands, yet its rhythm, team play and pony craft bore the imprint of Manipur’s Sagol Kangjei.

i18n.hi: जल्द ही कछार और असम में रेजिमेंटल पोलो क्लब बने। नई ज़मीनों में ब्रिटिश इस खेल को अपना बताने लगे, पर उसकी लय, टीम की चाल और टट्टुओं की हुनर पर मणिपुर के सगोल कंग्जेई की मुहर साफ़ थी।

panels.shot: intimate medium shot of Keifa Singh speaking quietly to a young Manipuri boy near the boundary rope
panels.action: Keifa Singh stands beside a boundary rope, hand resting on a pony’s neck, as he speaks to a wide-eyed Manipuri boy, the distant game playing on behind them.

dialogue.speaker: king_khagemba_and_keifa_singh
dialogue.text: Remember, we play first for each other, then for any king.

i18n.hi: याद रखो, हम पहले एक-दूसरे के लिए खेलते हैं, फिर किसी राजा के लिए।

panels.shot: wide, time-lapse style composition of the same ground shifting from Khagemba’s era to colonial times to a modern polo match
panels.action: The Imphal ground is shown in three ghosted layers: Khagemba-era horsemen with spears, nineteenth-century Manipuri and British riders together, and a modern polo match, all sharing the same strip of earth.

dialogue.text: Legends push Sagol Kangjei back into mythic ages, but the firm trail runs from Khagemba’s court, through exile and empire, into modern polo—its core preserved in a living ground and a living breed.

i18n.hi: किस्से सगोल कंग्जेई को मिथकीय युगों तक ले जाते हैं, पर पक्की राह खागेम्बा के दरबार से चलती है, निर्वासन और साम्राज्यों के बीच से गुजरकर आधुनिक पोलो तक—जिसका मूल जिंदा मैदान और जिंदा नस्ल में बचा है।

panels.shot: low-angle dusk shot of King Khagemba’s statue or imagined figure, outlined against the Kangla sky, echoed by distant modern riders
panels.action: At dusk, an idealised figure of King Khagemba stands in silhouette atop Kangla’s embankment, the faint silhouettes of riders circling in the background as ponies kick up dust in the fading light.

dialogue.text: Khagemba will be remembered for battles and treaties, but this quieter act endures: shaping a game where discipline and joy share the same field, a legacy that outlived the crowns that ordered it.

i18n.hi: खागेम्बा की याद में युद्ध और सन्धियाँ ज़्यादा गिनी जाएँगी, पर यह नरम काम ज़्यादा टिक गया: ऐसा खेल गढ़ना जहाँ अनुशासन और खुशी एक ही मैदान बाँटें, वह धरोहर जो उन ताजों से ज़्यादा जीती रही जिनके नाम पर बनी।

panels.shot: close-up on a Manipuri pony’s eye reflecting both Kangla walls and a faraway modern polo stadium
panels.action: The dark eye of a Manipuri pony fills the frame, its glossy surface reflecting the ancient walls of Kangla on one side and a distant, modern polo stadium on the other.

dialogue.text: Conquest drew borders that later vanished; Sagol Kangjei crossed them on four small hooves. Through Khagemba and riders like Keifa Singh, a people’s play traveled farther than any army’s march.

i18n.hi: फ़तहों ने जो सरहदें खींचीं, वो मिट गईं; सगोल कंग्जेई चार नन्हें खुरों पर उन्हें पार करता रहा। खागेम्बा और कैफ़ा सिंह जैसे सवारों से लोगों का खेल किसी भी फ़ौज से ज़्यादा दूर जा पहुँचा।

title_i18n.hi: सगोल कंग्जेई: कांगला से निकला पोलो

subtitle_i18n.en: From Kangla’s red earth to the world’s green fields
subtitle_i18n.hi: कांगला की लाल मिट्टी से दुनिया के हरे मैदानों तक
